angle: measurement side - what an EEG signal-quality index responds to: contamination versus neural state
study_sentence: Within-subject simulation experiment on 24 simulated subjects (seed sets with jittered network parameters) of a spiking thalamocortical EEG generator: after an assigned artifact-free change of neural state (predictor), the false-alarm rate of signal-quality indices thresholded on the baseline state (outcome) is compared with its nominal 5%, expressed as an equivalent dose of added recorded contamination, and repeated on eyes-closed versus eyes-open recordings.
question: How large is the false-alarm rate of EEG signal-quality indices on an artifact-free simulated EEG whose neural state alone has changed, and to what dose of contamination is that change equivalent?

original_question.text: How much do EEG signal-quality indices change when the neural state of an artifact-free simulated EEG changes, relative to their change under a known dose of contamination?
original_question.changed_because: restatement: the reader showed that a ratio at one arbitrary dose (a_0 = 0.3) and threshold (0.25) decides little; the question now asks for the false-alarm rate against each index's own detection threshold and for the equivalent dose

coverage.question: part
coverage.tested_part: how large the false-alarm rate of the within-recording composite signal-quality indices is on an artifact-free simulated EEG whose neural state alone has changed (against a threshold of 0.20)

untested.part: to what dose of contamination that change is equivalent

angle_parts.part: what an EEG signal-quality index responds to

claims.statement: Although signal-quality indices are read as measures of contamination, in an artifact-free simulated EEG a change of neural state of eyes-closed/eyes-open size raises the false-alarm rate of at least two of the three within-recording composite signal-quality indices (PREP-style, FASTER-style, Layer-Q), thresholded on the baseline state, to 0.20 or more (nominal 0.05), because these indices compare channels and epochs within the recording, and a state change alters that comparison with no contamination added.
reasons: Robust-z criteria compare each channel or epoch with the others of the same recording; a change of thalamic drive changes the between-channel and between-epoch distribution without adding any non-neural source.
On a signal with zero non-neural content every epoch above the threshold is a false alarm.

evidence.measure: false-alarm rate: 1-s epochs of 64-channel signal -> index Q_k per epoch -> indicator Q_k > tau_k (tau_k = 95th percentile of Q_k over the 60 epochs of a separate 60-s baseline-state calibration run of the same simulated subject) -> fraction of the 40 state-B epochs flagged per subject and index -> mean over 24 subjects per index -> FA2 = the second-largest of the three per-index rates (PREP-style, FASTER-style, Layer-Q), with one-sided 95% bootstrap bounds over subjects; the Riemannian-potato and single-feature rates are reported, not counted
evidence.would_show: a lower one-sided 95% bound of FA2 at or above 0.20
evidence.refuted_if: the upper one-sided 95% bootstrap bound of FA2 is below 0.20
evidence.can_fail: yes: the manipulation acts on the thalamic drive of all patches and the indices are computed per epoch on all 64 channels; criteria that compare channels within the recording may not move at all when every patch changes alike, and FA2 then stays near 0.05

evidence.measure: the same false-alarm rate on recordings: tau_k from each subject's eyes-closed epochs (first half), flagged fraction of eyes-open epochs without an EOG- or frontal-amplitude-detected ocular event, and of held-out eyes-closed epochs (nominal check), in ds004148 -> mean over 60 subjects per index -> second-largest of the three within-recording indices
evidence.would_show: a recorded false-alarm rate also at or above 0.20
evidence.refuted_if: E2 is supported but on recordings the upper one-sided 95% bound of the eyes-open false-alarm rate is below 0.20 - the simulated result is then not taken to hold for recorded EEG
evidence.can_fail: yes: eyes-open epochs may stay within the eyes-closed spread of the indices

construction.predictor_formula: s_B = G(theta_A with g_T -> g_T'), with P_alpha(s_B) / P_alpha(s_A) = rho_ECEO
construction.outcome_formula: FA2 = second largest over k in {PREP, FASTER, LayerQ} of mean over epochs e of 1[ Q_k(s_B, e) > tau_k ], tau_k = q95 over epochs of Q_k(s_A0), s_A0 a separate realisation of the state of s_A
construction.computable_without_experiment: partly: for the single-feature spectral indices and for the Riemannian-potato distance the direction of the shift follows from the definition and rho_ECEO or the baseline covariance, so they are excluded from FA2; for the three within-recording indices Q_k(s_B, e) depends on between-channel and between-epoch robust statistics of s_B, which exist only once s_B is simulated. s_B is the manipulated signal that the outcome scores; nothing about its robust-z statistics follows from the alpha ratio. s_A, the baseline state, defines the alpha ratio of the manipulation and (through its separate realisation s_A0) the thresholds; what that shared baseline alone produces is the rate of a second realisation of it, measured in E3 and expected at 0.05.
construction.free_quantity: whether a state change that affects all patches alike shifts the within-recording robust statistics beyond the epoch-to-epoch spread of the baseline state

claims.warrant: When a factor is assigned while every non-neural source is held at zero, and a score changes, then the score responds to that factor and not to contamination.
claims.warrant_basis: (field convention) - the logic of an assigned manipulation; the generator's zero non-neural content is by construction

outcomes.if_supported: we learn that within-recording quality criteria reject clean data after a state change, how often per index, and to what dose of real contamination that is equivalent
outcomes.if_not: we learn that these indices keep their nominal false-alarm rate across a state change of eyes-closed/eyes-open size, so a rise in flagged epochs between conditions indicates contamination

negation.text: After an eyes-closed/eyes-open-sized change of neural state at most one of the three within-recording indices flags one clean epoch in five.

expected_direction.basis: unknown: within-recording criteria are relative to the other channels and epochs, so a change that affects all patches alike may cancel, or may change the spread they are scaled by; the definitions do not say which

claims.smallest_effect_of_interest: FA2 = 0.20 (design choice: four times the nominal rate; one clean epoch in five rejected for a reason that is not contamination)
claims.falsifier: E2: the upper one-sided 95% bootstrap bound (24 simulated subjects) of FA2, the second-largest false-alarm rate of state-B epochs among the three within-recording composite indices, is below 0.20

rivals.how: the false alarms are a property of this simulator (identical patches, flat aperiodic slope, 20 Hz harmonic), not of EEG
two realisations of the same state differ in the indices by sampling alone
the drive change alters total power besides alpha, and amplitude-dependent criteria respond to that

s_B is both the manipulated signal and what is scored; a reference-based index (the potato) rises by definition when the state leaves its baseline; s_A is the state the manipulation departs from and the state the thresholds are taken from
a calibrated index's reference computed on the segments it scores
rivals.ruled_out_by: design: the reference comes from separate seeds

controls.negative: E3: a second realisation of the baseline state (A', new noise seeds) is scored in place of state B; expected rate 0.05 for every index (the indicator and the order statistic pass it through: second largest of three values near 0.05 is near 0.05, slightly above the mean). A gain-only arm, an RMS-matched state B and a notch at 18-22 Hz (the generator's alpha harmonic) are scored as well.
controls.negative_can_move: yes: A' is scored by the same indices on the same 64 channels against the same tau_k; a miscalibrated threshold or seed dependence moves it away from 0.05
controls.positive: E4: half of the A' epochs are replaced by state-A epochs with ocular or muscle contamination at a dose where the detection rate has saturated in E5
controls.positive_expected: each per-index rate = 0.5 * 1 + 0.5 * 0.05 = 0.525, so FA2 = 0.525: the indicator returns 1 for an epoch above tau_k whatever its size, so the planted value comes back only at a dose in the saturated part of that index's dose-response curve (E5 shows it first; at detection rate p the value is 0.5 p + 0.025), and the second-largest of three equal rates is that rate

scope.internal: for this generator, one state path (thalamic drive), thresholds from the baseline state, and three within-recording composite indices
scope.external: generalises to recorded EEG only as far as E6 agrees; does not generalise to other state changes (sleep, drugs), other indices, deep-learning quality classifiers or thresholds calibrated across states
limits: the claim is one-sided (flagged as worse); a state change that masks contamination is reported in E5, not tested
a threshold calibrated across both states bounds the rate near nominal by construction; that regime is reported, not tested
the Riemannian-potato distance rises by definition when the state leaves its baseline; its rate is reported, not counted
the because clause is a conjecture: no experiment separates the between-channel from the between-epoch route

power.unit: simulated subjects (independent seed sets with jittered network parameters)
power.min_detectable: d >= 0.51 at 80% power, one-sided alpha = 0.05 (paired / one-sample against 0.20; rough, n < 30)

claims.statement: For each of the seven signal-quality indices and each contamination class on the artifact-free simulated EEG, the dose-response of the detection rate, the smallest dose with a detection rate of 0.5, and the state-equivalent dose (the dose whose detection rate equals the false-alarm rate of the changed neural state) are estimated to within one step of a nine-step dose grid in 24 simulated subjects.
reasons: An index proposed as a validation anchor should respond monotonically to a known dose; where it starts to respond is its detection floor.

evidence.measure: index per 2-s epoch -> detection rate (fraction above tau_k) per dose, class and subject -> smallest dose with detection rate 0.5; dose whose detection rate equals the subject's state-B false-alarm rate (monotone interpolation); detection rate of the same doses added to state B -> median and interquartile range over subjects
evidence.would_show: a detection floor and an equivalent dose per index and class, and whether the changed state masks contamination

claims.warrant: When a known amount of a contaminant is added to a signal known to be clean, the change of a score is that score's response to the contaminant.

outcomes.if_supported: we learn each index's detection floor per contaminant class on a signal whose cleanliness is known
outcomes.if_not: we learn which indices are blind or non-monotonic for which class

claims.estimate_because: size-open: indices worsen with contamination by design, so the direction is settled; the dose at which each first responds is unknown

rivals.how: the dose scale (a = 1: as recorded relative to its source background) is tied to two source datasets, so equivalent doses are in those datasets' units

scope.internal: four contaminant classes at nine doses on this generator
scope.external: floors are relative to this generator's background amplitude and spectrum
limits: dose is an amplitude scale, not a rate of events

claims.precision_target: one step of the dose grid (aim); 24 subjects give an interquartile range per index and class

claims.statement: Although a signal without contamination should receive the best score, at least one of the signal-quality indices calibrated on recordings rates the artifact-free simulated EEG worse than the median recording, because such an index measures distance from the typical recording.
reasons: A reference-calibrated index is small for signals that resemble the reference set and large for those that do not, whatever the reason.

evidence.measure: index calibrated on ds004148 eyes-closed recordings -> value per simulated subject (24) and per held-out recording (60, split-half calibration) -> one-sided Mann-Whitney per index, Holm-corrected
evidence.would_show: at least one calibrated index for which the simulated EEG is not better than the median recording
evidence.refuted_if: every reference-calibrated index rates the simulated EEG better than the median recording (one-sided Mann-Whitney at alpha = 0.05, Holm-corrected)
evidence.can_fail: yes: the simulated EEG has no artifacts and may score best on all

claims.warrant: When a signal known to be free of contamination scores worse than recordings that are not, the score measures something other than contamination.

outcomes.if_supported: we learn that the best score is not reserved for the cleanest signal, and which index properties cost the simulated EEG its score
outcomes.if_not: we learn that calibrated indices do rank an artifact-free signal above recordings, which supports using a generator as their ceiling

negation.text: Every index calibrated on recordings rates the artifact-free simulated EEG better than the median recording.

expected_direction.basis: unknown: the simulated EEG lacks artifacts, which favours a better score, and differs from recordings in slope and topography, which favours a worse one

claims.falsifier: E7: every reference-calibrated index rates the simulated EEG better than the median recording (one-sided Mann-Whitney, 24 simulated vs 60 recorded, alpha = 0.05, Holm-corrected)

rivals.how: the simulated EEG scores worse because of generator defects that resemble contamination (the 20 Hz harmonic read as muscle), not because of atypicality as such

controls.negative: a held-out half of the recordings scored against the other half is expected at the median by construction
controls.negative_can_move: yes: the held-out recordings are scored by the same indices
controls.positive: simulated EEG with contamination at a = 1 must score worse than the clean simulated EEG
controls.positive_expected: a one-sided Mann-Whitney p below 0.05 for every calibrated index that passed the orientation check

scope.internal: this generator against ds004148 eyes-closed recordings
limits: a worse score may reflect generator defects

power.min_detectable: standardized difference of about 0.6 at 80% power (two-group 24 vs 60, one-sided; rough)

sample.target: resting scalp EEG of adults in distinct neural states
sample.accessible: 24 simulated subjects of one generator, and 90 recorded adults in E6
sample.concern: identical cortical patches, no cortico-cortical coupling, flat aperiodic slope

predictor.phenomenon: a change of neural state with no change of contamination
predictor.variable: thalamic background drive set so that the alpha-power ratio equals the eyes-closed / eyes-open ratio of ds004148
predictor.validity: construct: the alpha change of eye opening is the best-documented resting state change; the path through thalamic drive is one of several that could produce it

outcome.phenomenon: what a recording-level quality score responds to
outcome.variable: seven label-free indices, oriented larger = worse
outcome.accuracy: unit-tested against the published definitions; not cross-checked against reference implementations (not installed)
outcome.validity: content: covers covariance-distance, robust-z, amplitude and spectral families; classifier-based indices are missing

tradeoffs.change: a test of the state response of the three single-feature spectral indices was not written
tradeoffs.because: their response follows from their definitions and the imposed alpha ratio (by-construction check, step 3)
tradeoffs.lost: a pass/fail decision for these three indices; their responses are still reported in E2
tradeoffs.why: the question is answered on the indices whose response is not derivable

tradeoffs.change: the primary statistic was replaced: the median absolute state-to-contamination ratio at one dose (threshold 0.25) became the false-alarm rate of state-B epochs against each index's own baseline threshold (threshold 0.20, one-sided); E3, E4 and E6 were rebuilt for the new statistic, and E6 now uses the recorded eyes-closed to eyes-open change
tradeoffs.because: reader doubts 1, 2, 3 and 5: the ratio depended on an arbitrary reference dose, was unsigned, summarised by a median, and E6 measured another quantity
tradeoffs.lost: a single number comparing the state response with the contamination response at a fixed dose; the comparison survives as the state-equivalent dose of C2, estimated and not tested
tradeoffs.why: the old question asked for a ratio to a known dose; the study now tests a false-alarm rate and estimates the equivalent dose, so the question was reworded (original_question); the gap (specificity to contamination untested) and the angle are still what the study addresses

tradeoffs.change: C2 now also estimates the state-equivalent dose and the masking of contamination by the changed state
tradeoffs.because: the fixed-dose comparison left the primary claim (doubt 1)

tradeoffs.change: RMS-matching of state B was moved from the primary arm to a reported arm
tradeoffs.because: reader doubt 4: rescaling is not what a state change does
tradeoffs.why: the unmatched state is the natural manipulation; the gain-only arm separates amplitude

tradeoffs.change: the Riemannian-potato distance left the decision statistic, which became the second-largest rate among the three within-recording indices; thresholds now come from a separate 60-s calibration run with 1-s epochs; E3 gained a notch arm for the 20 Hz harmonic
tradeoffs.because: restatement-2 doubts 2, 3, 5 and 7 (forced revision of the finalize round)
tradeoffs.lost: a decision on the reference-based index; its rate is still reported
tradeoffs.why: the question asks for the false-alarm rate of quality indices after a state change; the test now rests on the indices whose response is not given by their definition

reader_doubts.doubt: 1. the ratio and its 0.25 threshold depend on an arbitrary reference dose a_0 = 0.3 on a dose scale tied to two datasets
reader_doubts.how: C1 and E2 changed: the statistic is the false-alarm rate against each index's own baseline threshold, with no reference dose; the dose comparison moved to C2 (E5) as an estimated state-equivalent dose

reader_doubts.doubt: 2. for reference-calibrated indices a nonzero response follows from the definition, and the calibration state was not given
reader_doubts.how: C1 changed to a magnitude test (direction-settled, threshold 0.20) and E1/E2 now state the calibration of every index: potato reference and thresholds from the baseline state, three of the four composite indices self-referential; the mixed-state regime is reported as a scope limit

reader_doubts.doubt: 3. the statistic is unsigned and a median over four indices can pass with two indices responding
reader_doubts.how: C1 and E2 changed: one-sided false-alarm rate (flagged as worse), mean over the four composite indices, per-index rates reported; masking is estimated in E5

reader_doubts.doubt: 4. the simulated state change may not resemble a real one; RMS-matching is not what eye opening does; the target alpha ratio may be unreachable
reader_doubts.how: E2 changed: the unmatched state B is primary and the RMS-matched and gain-only arms are reported in E3; E0 gains a go/no-go check on the reachable alpha ratio; resemblance to recordings is carried by E6

reader_doubts.doubt: 5. E6 measures a different quantity (high- vs low-alpha epochs over blink vs no-blink epochs) and is only an upper bound
reader_doubts.how: E6 changed: it computes the same false-alarm rate on the recorded eyes-closed to eyes-open change of ds004148, with held-out eyes-closed epochs as the nominal check; it remains an upper bound because eyes-open epochs can hold undetected ocular activity

reader_doubts.doubt: 6. the 24 subjects are seed sets of one network, so the interval reflects simulation noise, and power is marginal
reader_doubts.how: E0 changed: each simulated subject gets its own connectivity seed and network parameters jittered by 10% (weights, drives), so the spread is between simulated individuals; that it is not variability between people stays in the scope limits

reader_doubts.doubt: 7. indices are own implementations and may not match the published ones
reader_doubts.how: E1 changed: pyprep and autoreject (pure Python, not installed today) are installed and the PREP-style criteria are cross-checked against pyprep on ds004148 before use

reader_doubts.doubt: 8. decision rules are fixed only by a local commit hash
reader_doubts.how: E0 says fixed before analysis, not externally timestamped, and the labelled risk entry is added

reader_doubts.doubt: 9. C3 is never stated and its rule does not say which claim it refutes
reader_doubts.how: E7 now states the claim it tests in full

reader_doubts.doubt: 1. a supported result may be a property of the generator; E6 can veto but not corroborate
reader_doubts.how: data: no recording on this machine has a change of neural state with independently verified zero contamination - the phantom ds004784 has no neural state, and in ds004148 eyes-open epochs can hold undetected ocular activity

reader_doubts.doubt: 2. the primary test is close to true by construction for the reference-based index (potato) and thresholds set on the baseline state
reader_doubts.how: C1 and E2 changed: the potato distance is outside the decision statistic, which now rests on the three within-recording indices, for which no direction is predicted

reader_doubts.doubt: 3. fifteen epochs per condition make the 95th-percentile threshold and the negative control unreliable, and it is unclear which epochs set the threshold
reader_doubts.how: E0 and E2 changed: 1-s epochs; thresholds from a separate 60-s baseline calibration run (60 epochs); A' and B are 40 s each (40 epochs)

reader_doubts.doubt: 4. 24 jittered copies of one network are not between-person variability; power is marginal; the 0.20 cut-off is not justified
reader_doubts.how: data: no measured between-person distribution of this generator's parameters exists on this machine to sample subjects from; the cut-off stays a labelled design choice

reader_doubts.doubt: 5. a mean over four indices can be carried by one; three of four are own implementations
reader_doubts.how: C1 and E2 changed: the statistic is the second-largest per-index rate among three, so two indices must reach the threshold; implementations other than PREP-style remain uncross-checked (risk entry)

reader_doubts.doubt: 6. the equivalent dose is on a scale tied to two source datasets and E4 depends on E5 finding a saturated dose
reader_doubts.how: data: no artifact library on this machine has a dose scale independent of its source recording; E4's dependence on E5 is stated in its entry

reader_doubts.doubt: 7. the 20 Hz harmonic may vary with the state change and bear on E2
reader_doubts.how: E3 changed: harmonic power is reported for both states and E2's rates are recomputed after an 18-22 Hz notch

reader_doubts.doubt: 8. decision rules only in a local commit; novelty rests on titles and abstracts
reader_doubts.how: both are stated as labelled risk entries
